title: Known gaps & limitations
intro: This page separates missing cited pages, unresolved source readings, distinct package offers, and work still under review. It does not claim complete coverage of the books. A page reference shows where a record points; it does not prove that every field on the record comes from that page.

entries.title: Bo Stick · Purchase price
entries.description: No purchase-price row for Bo Stick was found in the inspected PHB p.35 or p.123 cost tables or the UA p.26 cost table. PHB p.37 and UA p.26 list its number under Approximate Weight in Gold Pieces, which is encumbrance rather than purchase cost. A price outside these bounded lists has not been ruled out. A separate editorial estimate is 5 sp for one bo stick; it is not a printed price. A plain wooden staff is assumed to require less manufacture than the PHB p.35 spear at 1 gp (20 sp) or UA p.26 sap at 1 gp. The 5 sp figure is a discretionary quarter of either comparator, not a printed bo-stick price.

entries.title: Club · Purchase price
entries.description: No purchase-price row for Club was found in the inspected PHB p.35 or p.123 cost tables or the UA p.26 cost table. PHB p.37, PHB p.124, and UA p.26 show its number under a weapon-weight column, not a purchase-price column. A price outside these bounded lists has not been ruled out. A separate editorial estimate is 2 sp for one club; it is not a printed price. Assumes a simply shaped purchased wooden club; the UA p.26 sap is 1 gp (20 sp). A lower 2 sp suggestion is a judgment about simple materials and workmanship, not a printed club price or a rule preventing scavenging a club.

entries.title: Quarterstaff · Purchase price
entries.description: No purchase-price row for Quarterstaff was found in the inspected PHB p.35 or p.123 cost tables or the UA p.26 cost table. The PHB p.124 and UA p.26 entries labelled Staff, Quarter are in weapon-weight tables, not purchase-price tables. A price outside these bounded lists has not been ruled out. A separate editorial estimate is 5 sp for one quarterstaff; it is not a printed price. Assumes a plain prepared wooden staff, without a metal point; the PHB p.35 spear is 1 gp (20 sp) and UA p.26 staff sling is 2 gp (40 sp). The 5 sp suggestion is an arbitrary lower price, not a printed quarterstaff price.

entries.title: Sling Stone · Purchase price
entries.description: No purchase-price row for Sling Stone was found in the inspected PHB p.35 or p.123 cost tables or the UA p.26 cost table. The PHB p.124 and UA p.26 entries labelled Sling Stone are in weapon-weight tables. The PHB p.35 “Sling & Bullets, dozen” offer (15 sp) and “Sling Bullets, score” offer (10 sp) are distinct packages and do not state a stone price. A separate editorial estimate is 1 sp for 20 selected sling stones; it is not a printed price. The PHB p.35 lists 20 sling bullets for 10 sp. This suggestion assumes a purchased, selected set of 20 stones costs less than manufactured bullets; 1 sp is a discretionary package price, not a printed stone price. Suitable stones might instead be gathered at the DM's discretion.

entries.title: Magic-user · Magic Mirror · Scrying detection
entries.description: Recorded source conflict for this field; the status does not claim that every reading is a proven book contradiction. Check each round. The DMG states an Intelligence 12+ minimum, but its spell-user detection table contains lower-Intelligence entries; how these interact is unresolved. For non-spell-users, base chances are fighter 2%, paladin 6%, ranger 4%, thief 6%, assassin 5%, monk 1%, bard 3%; UA adds cavalier 5% and barbarian 1%. Add 1% per experience level and cumulative Intelligence bonuses above 12: 13–18 give +1%, +3%, +6%, +10%, +15%, +21% respectively. Treat monsters as the most applicable class. Spell-users use the detection-of-invisibility table instead.

entries.title: PHB and DMG discovery census
entries.description: A bounded 370-page PHB/DMG discovery census recorded 52 page/group claims and 18 declared source groups. Structured output exists for 18 declared groups, covering 179 logical records. Transcription, focus/context review and item-citation mapping are separate; the linked review queue records their current status. Text-screened noncandidate and unreviewed pages do not establish that no price exists. This is a monetary discovery census, not a source-row transcription or whole-book semantic completeness claim. The 370-page denominator counts only the PHB and DMG PDFs. The separate DMG printed-p.175 image is a supplement and is excluded from that count. Counts distinguish screened pages, visually screened thumbnails, and previously inventoried scoped pages; these are not interchangeable denominators. Starting wealth, currency conversion, ordinary purchase prices, hireling wages, service fees, construction costs, spell/component costs, treasure generation, market valuations and item values are typed separately rather than treated as equivalent “prices.” Any exact amount in discoverySummary or locatorAmountCue is a locator note only pending source-scale verification; it must not be consumed as a normalized/verified source fact.

entries.title: UA discovery census
entries.description: A bounded 130-page UA census recorded 65 discovery claims and 15 declared source groups. Structured output exists for 15 declared groups, covering 583 logical records. Transcription, focus/context review and item-citation mapping are separate; the linked review queue records their current status. The basic equipment table is covered by a separate scoped inventory. The source census is additional to the existing p.26 equipment table inventory; that page is not duplicated. No whole-book visual-completeness claim: many noncandidate pages are text-screen-only and OCR/text screening can miss currency values. Table rows and object/value pairings for the random magic-item price tables are not fully transcribed. Bounds are deliberately whole-page and page-level only. Every recorded claim was visually associated with its source page, but fine-grained claim-specific rectangles were not measured. The printed-p.97 continuation has a visible value but unresolved object identity. Sale value, component value, creation price, repair fee, treasure cap, behavior threshold, weight, and starting wealth remain typed distinctly; they are not interchangeable claims.
